correctness.rationale: For W=A∪C the only alternatives swap in b; their score changes are p/(r+1)-q/k on dropping a C candidate and -h/r-q/k on dropping an A candidate. This proves both optimality and the strict uniqueness criterion. Definition 4, Eq. (6) in Skowron specializes to the displayed strict payment test including the nonwinner and also allows coalition members who do not approve it. For any coalition of counts x,y,z with x>0 and z>0, a C-type voter's payment r/(x+y+z)+s/max(x,z) exceeds k/n. For z=0, the group maximum is r/(x+y)+1/x, minimized at x=p,y=h. In the core and standard EJR+ tests no one outside the p-type can improve, and the p-type can afford fewer than r+1 seats since q≥pk/(r+1) and n>q. For sharpness, t=(p+h)/p, z=q/p give k/(r+1)≤z≤k+r-(t+r)-kr/(t+r)≤(sqrt(k)-sqrt(r))². The resulting k bound is >11 for r=1,2 and at least 12 for r≥3 (the stated derivative is positive). The explicit witness gives q/k=2+1/k, payment 7/24, and entitlement k/(2k+17)>7/24 iff 10k>119. Independently enumerating all 13 exclusions and the 1716 coalition signatures with exact fractions at k=12 gave a PAV gap 1/12, sole blocking count vector (6,10,0), and deficit 1/984. To verify the broad lower-bound wording for all PAV optima, dropping an A member cannot be optimal; a committee omitting c∈C instead of b always passes the strong test: in a coalition with z>0 supporters of c, a C-type voter pays r/(x+y+z)+s/z≥r/n+s/q>k/n. Thus there is no hidden alternative-committee counterexample, including ties or s=1.

value.rationale: This settles a natural rule-versus-axiom question rather than another axiom-versus-axiom test. The unique winner avoids tie-breaking artifacts; the exact inequalities explain when the shared approvals and bloc sizes create a violation and why the first possible seat size in the model is twelve. Core and standard EJR+ compatibility isolate the stronger payment requirement as the cause.
